actionItems: Jana and Francine will co-create a remote prototype using modelling clay by the next meeting
UI/UX team will develop the user interface design by the next meeting
Marketing expert will conduct product evaluation by the next meeting
keyPoints: Remote uses push buttons only, not scroll wheels or advanced switches, due to cost and simplicity.
Voice recognition is the primary differentiator and must be context-specific (e.g., 'Good morning' triggers TV to turn on).
Design prioritizes visual appeal with a trendy, compact, colorful, and soft-touch feel inspired by fruit and vegetable shapes.
Remote will be battery-powered, with IR transmission and a T-shaped form factor for child safety and usability.
Key features include channel navigation, volume control, mute, and a display for program timing.
summary.summary: The team finalized a push-button remote with voice recognition as the key feature, emphasizing visual appeal, simplicity, and child-friendly design. The remote will feature a colorful, soft-touch, fruit/vegetable-inspired aesthetic, be battery-powered, and include essential functions like on/off, volume, and channel navigation. Voice recognition is highlighted as a differentiator, though its implementation requires further cost and performance analysis.
summary.title: Remote Control Design Finalized
